layout_dets.text: THE CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF THE PASSIVE FILM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ON Fe-24Cr AND Fe-24Cr-11Mo STUDIED BY AES, XPS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AND SIMS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S. MISCHLER, A. VOGEL, H. J. MATHIEU and D. LANDOLT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Materials Department, Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (EPFL), CH-1007 Lausanne, Switzerland

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—A systematic study of the composition and of the thickness of passive films formed at 65°C on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fe-24Cr and Fe-24Cr-11Mo model alloys in an acid sulfate electrolyte in the presence and absence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ion at different potentials has been carried out. Non-destructive XPS, AES depth profiling and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamic SIMS were applied to the study of the average concentration and the depth distribution of cations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and anions in the films. The apparent film thickness and the average metal ion concentration were found to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be little affected by the presence or absence of chloride ion in the electrolyte. Molybdenum influenced the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth distribution of chloride ion in the films.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SrAinLEss steels owe their corrosion resistance to the presence of a thin surface oxide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film. The characterization of such films, therefore, is an important field of corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: science. Surface analysis methods, in particular AES, XPS and SIMS have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied to the study of the chemical composition of passive oxide films on stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels for a number of years and results obtained by different research groups have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been reviewed in the literature. 1.2 It is generally accepted that passive oxide films on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iron-chromium alloys consist predominantly of trivalent chromium oxide.³ Their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness is 2–3 nm typically and depends on applied potential.ª The presence in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: films of cations of iron, of molybdenum or of other alloying elements has also been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: documented depending on alloy composition.⁵-7 Incorporation of chloride ions has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been observed by some authors but not by others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Molybdenum is frequently added to ferritic and austenitic stainless steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve their resistance to pitting corrosion in chloride media. It is not known at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present whether passive films on molybdenum containing alloys formed in chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: media have the same composition as those formed in other media and how they differ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from films on similar alloys not containing molybdenum. Such information could

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possibly be of use for the elucidation of pit initiation mechanisms on stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the role of molybdenum in this.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most of the published studies of passive films use only one surface analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method and cover a limited range of experimental conditions. Results, however, are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more easily interpreted when they can be compared on a relative basis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Preferably, they ought to be substantiated by different analysis techniques. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these reasons, a study was initiated in our laboratory with the aim of providing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive set of experimental data for the determination of the influence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied potential, of alloyed molybdenum and of the presence of chloride ion in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte on the composition and thickness of the passive films formed on

layout_dets.text: EXPERIMENTAL METHOD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The composition of the two alloys used is given in Table 1. The Fe-24Cr–11Mo alloy contained a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher molybdenum concentration than the usual ferritic stainless steels in order to facilitate analysis of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this element in the passive film. The alloys which are single phase were heat treated at 1300°C for 58 h to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homogenize the elemental concentration. Grain size after heat treatment was in the millimeter range. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys contained a few chromium oxide inclusions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The electrodes were machined in the form of rods from which rotating disk electrodes were fabricated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For the determination of polarization curves the disk electrode of 3.57 mm diameter (electrode area

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was embedded in epoxy. For potentiostatic measurements involving surface analysis identical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrodes were used but without epoxy insulation. By bringing the disk into contact with the electrolyte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface and slightly pulling back, a meniscus was formed which prevented contact of the side of the rod

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the electrolyte. The rotation rate was 3000 rpm in all experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two electrolytes were used, 0.1 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: referred to as electrolyte A and 0.1 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NaCl referred to as electrolyte B. All experiments were carried out in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: de-aerated solutions under argon. The temperature was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This temperature was chosen because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preliminary experiments had shown that passive films formed at that temperature were slightly thicker

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than those formed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and thus easier to study. At the temperature of the experiments the Fe-Cr alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but not the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy exhibited pitting in the electrolyte B.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrode pretreatment consisted of mechanical polishing with SiC paper and with 1 μm alumina

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: powder. The electrodes were washed with ethanol and doubly distilled water before being used.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Polarization curves were determined by applying potential steps and plotting the current measured after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 400 s. The measurements were started at a cathodic potential of –650 mV (all potentials in this paper are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given with respect to the normal hydrogen electrode). A potentiostat (Solartron 1286) controlled by a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: function generator (AMEL 568) was used. Electrodes used for surface analysis were mechanically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polished and polarized potentiostatically. Three polarization conditions were studied; the condition (CA)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involved cathodic polarization at -650 mV for 1 min. The polarization condition (PL) involved cathodic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarization at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 1 min followed by anodic polarization for 1 h at 200 mV. The polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: condition (PH) was the same as (PL) but anodic polarization was at 500 mV. The current was monitored as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a function of time using an HP 310 computer. At the end of a polarization experiment the electrode was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: removed from the electrolyte with the potential still applied, rinsed with doubly distilled water and dried

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with argon. It was stored in a desiccator under argon for a maximum of 2 h before being introduced into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the surface analysis apparatus and immediately analysed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The characterization of passive films by AES, XPS and SIMS is subject to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitations inherent in all ex situ methods.¹ An important consideration, therefore, is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S. MIsCHLER et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to what extent results are affected by the rinsing and sample transfer procedures used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and what reproducibility can be achieved. The former point has been discussed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elsewhere.15,18 Suffice here to mention that SIMS experiments performed with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isotope indicate that at potentials (PH) the post-oxidation of passive films is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: negligible. For the potentials (PL) such experiments are not available but it may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reasonably supposed that the behavior is similar. The presented data for (PH) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (PL), therefore, are believed to be representative of the passive film. The (CA) data,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the other hand, represent the film formed in air during rinsing and transfer and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their reproducibility is limited. It is clear from a comparison of the results that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical composition of the two types of films differs substantially.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Three parameters were varied in the present study: the potential, alloyed Mo and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the presence of Cl⁻ in the electrolyte. The observed influence of applied potential on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film thickness in the passive region (Fig. 5) and on the Mo content of the films (Fig. 6)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is in qualitative agreement with the literature2,7 although observed differences

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between (PL) and (PH) are slight. Alloyed Mo under the present conditions does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: affect the thickness of the passive film in a significant way (Fig. 5), but it alters its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition because of incorporation of Mo (Fig. 6). The growth-dissolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior of the passive films as revealed by the measured current-time transients

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Fig. 3) is apparently the same in presence and absence of alloyed Mo. This indicates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that at the potentials applied in this study the electrochemical properties of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film are not significantly affected by the molybdenum. In all experiments the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied potentials were well below the critical pitting potential and no current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instabilities of the type associated in the literature with metastable pitting19 were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed in this study.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The presence of chloride ion in the electrolyte had little effect on the measured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness of the passive films, although the data of Fig. 5 suggest that films formed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte B are slightly thinner. The electrolyte composition apparently affects the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution of molybdenum in the films; more molybdenum was found in the outer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: part of the film formed in electrolyte A than in electrolyte B as is evidenced by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ratio profiles Mo/Fe + Cr + Mo of Fig. 10.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The XPS, AES and SIMS data suggest that under the conditions of the present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study electrolyte anions are incorporated into the passive films formed on Fe-24Cr

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Fe-24Cr-11Mo. The presence of sulfate is deduced from XPS and AES, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of Cl⁻ from all three methods. The distribution of these species in the film is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not uniform, however, they are concentrated in the outer part of the film. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness of the chloride containing region of the passive films can be estimated from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 15 taking the 50% value of the maximum amplitude of the Cl⁻ profile as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measure. One obtains in this way 0.5 nm (PL) and 0.8 nm (PH), respectively for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fe-24Cr alloy, 0.4 nm (PL) and 0.7 nm (PH), respectively, for the Fe–24Cr–11Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy. Since the overall film thickness at a given potential is comparable for the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys it is concluded that Mo affects the chloride ion distribution in the film relatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more than the overall film thickness. A similar effect of Mo on the sulfur profile at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential (PH) appears in Fig. 12.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Different interpretations of the observed concentration-depth distribution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ion, are a priori possible. Firstly, surface analysis methods such as AES,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XPS and SIMS yield average values of concentration over the analysed area which in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the present study is 200 × 200 µm for AES, 700 × 700 μm for SIMS and 3 × 3 mm for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XPS. It cannot be excluded that on a smaller scale the concentration is non-uniform.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, if the films contain pores or defects of nanometer size, adsorption of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte anions at the pore walls could possibly lead to the observation of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration profile over a finite thickness. In the present case, this is unlikely,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: however, because one would expect to find the concentration maximum at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface rather than at some distance from it (Figs 8 and 9). Another possible way to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpret the observed chloride profiles is by postulating trapping of anions in a gel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like outer film consisting of precipitated hydroxides. Such a hypothesis is in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contradiction with the SIMS data of Fig. 14, however. They show only adsorbed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydroxyl ions but no hydroxide film of a thickness of several atomic layers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A third and perhaps more plausible interpretation is that electrolyte anions are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truly incorporated into the passive film where they can occupy positions of oxygen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions. This poses no conceptual difficulties in the case of chloride ions,20,21 but is more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difficult to visualize for sulfate. The structure of the passive films on the alloys used is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not known but according to McBee and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the films are expected to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amorphous. An amorphous structure is expected to facilitate the accommodation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte anions but the problem needs further elucidation. If electrolyte anions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are incorporated into the film one may ask why they are located predominantly in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outer part and why molybdenum affects their depth-distribution. At present no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfactory explanation for this behavior is available. According to Takahashi et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al. ,23 who studied anodic films on aluminium in a phosphate electrolyte, the extent of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporation of electrolyte anions in the outer part of the barrier film depends on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transference number of the metal ions in the oxide. Passive films on Fe-Cr and Fe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr-Mo alloys are believed to be n-type semi-conductors.24,25 Another approach,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore, might consider the effect of Mo on the space charge in the film.26 Further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studies using in situ experimental techniques will be needed to elucidate these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: questions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CONCLUSIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Surface analysis data obtained by AES, XPS and SIMS on passive films formed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under well defined electrochemical conditions in the presence and absence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ions on two ferritic iron-chromium alloys with and without molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lead to the following conclusions which are strictly valid for the experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions of this study.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) Alloyed molybdenum has only a minor effect on the thickness of the passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film and on its growth-dissolution kinetics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) The presence or absence of chloride ion in the electrolyte does not signifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cantly change the average metal ion concentration in the film and has only a minor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect on the film thickness.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3) Molybdenum and chloride ions rather than being distributed uniformly in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film are concentrated in its outer part.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (4) Alloyed molybdenum influences the chloride distribution in the film.
